terms.comment: Recorded by Morgan–Owens; applied to the sand sieve.

evidence: Plin. NH 18.115: farīnam crībrō (Lewis & Short s.v. cernō)
terms.comment: Cernere is first of all to separate, to sift (Lewis & Short), with the sieve in the ablative or with per.

evidence: Cato Agr. 25: vīnāceōs cotīdiē recentīs succernitō

phrases.latin: Farīnam, pulverem fermentārium, nitrum, salem per crībrum in catīnum trānsmittitō
phrases.english: Sieve the flour, baking powder, soda, and salt into a bowl

phrases.latin: deinde crībrum farīnārium pūrum sūmitō cāseumque per crībrum facitō trānseat in mortārium
phrases.english: then take a clean flour sieve and push the cheese through the sieve into the bowl

phrases.latin: nam iste quidem gradus succrētust crībrō pollināriō
phrases.english: why, that pace of yours has been sifted through a flour sieve

sources: Lewis & Short: cribrum · Lewis & Short: cerno · Lewis & Short: succerno
Theodōrus et pater: Culīna Theodōrī, the recipe book that goes with the libellī (Ad Libellōs I–VII); examples marked “Culīna Theodōrī” quote it word for word.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 379.
